what_it_does: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG—a technique where an LLM is first given relevant documents before answering questions) relies on approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANNS) to quickly find similar vectors in a database. ANNS is fast but inherently low-accuracy, missing relevant documents and degrading LLM output quality. Exact nearest-neighbor search is more accurate but requires comparing the query against every single vector—computationally prohibitive at scale. This paper proposes DReX, a two-stage hardware accelerator: an in-DRAM processing unit (logic directly in the memory chip itself) performs a coarse comparison using centroid distance, eliminating far-away vectors without transferring their full embeddings to the processor, then an outside-DRAM near-memory accelerator runs exact k-nearest-neighbor on only the filtered survivors. This two-level filtering dramatically reduces data movement while achieving exact retrieval.
